summary: Assembly District 28 spans parts of Santa Cruz and Santa Clara counties. Incumbent Democrat Gail Pellerin, Santa Cruz County's former longtime chief elections officer, was first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024 with 66.9%. In the June 2 primary she took 72.0%; Republican Carol Pefley, a former journalist and realtor, took 28.0%.

positions.stance: Co-authored AB 2839, the 2024 law restricting deceptive AI deepfakes near an election, which a federal court has since blocked. See her profile for her full legislative record. (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)
Wants to revise recent state housing laws to protect the character of Santa Cruz. (Lookout Santa Cruz op-ed, September 2026)

key_differences: Pefley's campaign centers on rolling back recent state housing laws. This research did not compile Pellerin's housing votes, so check her profile and roll calls before treating the contrast as settled.
Through May 16, 2026, Pellerin reported about $422,000 in contributions. Pefley reported about $47,000 plus a $10,000 loan (Transparency USA).
The district is safely Democratic by registration and recent results.
